topic: Stage 5 Expansion Phase 1 (Train 7) - Bechtel EPC and LNTP (May 2026)
wiki_text: In May 2026, Cheniere Energy Partners' subsidiary Sabine Pass Liquefaction Stage V, LLC (SPLV) signed a lump-sum turnkey EPC contract with Bechtel Energy for Phase 1 of the SPL Expansion Project, covering a single liquefaction train (Train 7, >6 mtpa expected total production), a boil-off gas re-liquefaction unit, and tie-ins to the existing Sabine Pass terminal, and issued Bechtel a Limited Notice to Proceed (LNTP) for early engineering and procurement. FERC and DOE non-FTA applications remain pending; FERC issued a draft EIS for the expansion. Cheniere expects to reach a final investment decision on Phase 1 by early 2027. The overall SPL Expansion is sized for up to ~20 mtpa peak across the trains; Phase 1 is Train 7, with Trains 8-9 in Phase 2.

topic: Energy Transfer suspends Lake Charles LNG development (Dec 2025)
wiki_text: On 18 December 2025, Energy Transfer LP announced it was suspending development of the Lake Charles LNG export project to redirect capital toward its natural gas pipeline backlog, which it judged to offer a superior risk/return profile. The announcement came after the company had appeared on the brink of an early-2026 FID, having pursued an ~80% equity sell-down (described by co-CEO Marshall McCrea as 'the last big, most important box'), a non-binding April 2025 HOA with MidOcean Energy (30% of construction cost / 30% offtake), and offtake deals with Shell (~2.1 mtpa) and Chevron (2 mtpa). DOE had earlier (Aug 2025) granted additional time to commence non-FTA exports after the prior 16 Dec 2025 export-start deadline became unachievable. Energy Transfer said it remains open to third-party interest in developing the project. The export project is variously described as ~16.45-16.5 mtpa nameplate across three trains (FERC/DOE authorization references 17.8 mtpa).

topic: Monkey Island LNG project revival - FEED and liquefaction technology (2025)
wiki_text: In September 2025 the revived Monkey Island LNG project (Cameron Parish, Louisiana; ~$25 billion, ~26 mtpa across two phases) selected ConocoPhillips' Optimized Cascade liquefaction process and awarded McDermott a Master Services Agreement for front-end engineering and planning. The developers plan Phase 1 of three trains (~5.2 mtpa each, ~15.6 mtpa combined) with two additional trains in a later phase to reach ~26 mtpa. Engineering and permitting were expected to begin in 2026, with first LNG targeted for the early 2030s.

topic: Plaquemines brownfield expansion - FERC filing and scope growth (2025)
wiki_text: On 17 November 2025 Venture Global filed its FERC application for the Plaquemines LNG brownfield expansion; FERC staff accepted the application into the formal Certificate Proceeding phase on 26 November 2025 (Docket CP26-27-000), and Venture Global filed corresponding DOE export-authorization applications. The expansion is to be built incrementally and has grown from an originally announced 24 liquefaction trains ('at least 18.6 mtpa') to 32 modular trains adding 'over 30.0 mtpa' of peak production after additional blocks were added in July 2025. GEM tracks the expansion as 'Expansion (T37-60)' (24 trains, 17.78 mtpa nameplate, proposed); the larger 32-train scope and peak-vs-nameplate capacity framing remain to be reconciled.

terminal_name: West Delta LNG Deepwater Port Terminal
topic: MARAD terminates West Delta LNG deepwater-port license application (2025)
wiki_text: In late 2025 the U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) terminated/denied the West Delta LNG deepwater-port license application (offshore Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana; six modular trains, ~5-6.1 mtpa). MARAD had required a complete amended application by 24 September 2025; applicant LNG21, having received eight extensions since December 2019, failed to submit a viable application, leading to denial. GEM currently lists the project as shelved (2025); the formal application termination is a candidate for cancelled status.
